audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers disagreed with the packet chart, with their own whys prose, and with the already-written nautilus__yorick mirror. win[0]/phases[0].side said Skill while whys[0] says 'Level 1 is yours'; win[3]/phases[3].side said Skill while whys[3] says 'Level 4 favors Nautilus'; the mirror sets Levels 2 and 3 to Nautilus and Level 6 to Yorick.
audit.why: Level 1 is Yorick's one clean window because Dredge Line does not exist yet. From 2 through 5 Nautilus owns it — a 1150-range hook on 14s, Titan's Wrath on a flat 12s, Riptide slowing every 7s and Staggering Blow rooting on his first auto. Level 6 flips it back permanently: Eulogy of the Isles out-sustains his shielded burst and he has no escape once he has committed.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Yorick / Nautilus / Nautilus / Nautilus / Yorick / Yorick / Yorick across win[0..6] and phases[0..6].side as one paired group, ratings 6/4/4/3/6/7/7. whys[1] and whys[2] rewritten; whys[0], whys[3] and whys[4] already matched.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-4 Nautilus spike was described with no cooldown numbers, and no spike named Depth Charge's cooldown.
audit.why: Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s and Riptide is 7s falling to 5s — that is why levels 3-5 are a continuous Nautilus window rather than a single burst. Depth Charge is 120/100/80s and hits one target, which is why it stops mattering against a Yorick who is split with Maiden.
audit.corrected: phases[2], phases[3] and phases[6] keyed to Riptide's 7s, Titan's Wrath and Depth Charge's 80s rank-3 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] told the player to 'Wall his Q hook and dredge escapes with W Dark Procession'. That is backwards and is the single most damaging line on the page.
audit.why: Riot's Dredge Line text: 'Colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it.' Dark Procession summons terrain. Caging a Nautilus therefore hands him a guaranteed reposition — he hooks your own wall and lands where he wants, cage or not. The correct rule is to place the wall behind him on his retreat path, never between you and him. The rest of the chain is also unstated: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against a target, which sets Riptide (7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, 600 range) and the follow-up, and Titan's Wrath (flat 12s) shields the whole exchange.
audit.corrected: wants.you[1] rewritten to 'Cage his retreat, never terrain he can hook to escape'; the same rule added to breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, phases[3].why and phases[5].why. Staggering Blow's root named in dontsFull[1].d and dontsFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: sequencingCues 0 — no 'wait for X before you Y' line anywhere.
audit.why: Dredge Line's 14s cooldown is the whole trade clock; without the number the advice to 'track it' is unactionable.
audit.corrected: The 14s hook cooldown and the 7s Riptide now appear in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, phases[1].why and phases[5].why with an explicit ordering.

notes: The most important correction here is wants.you[1]. Riot's Dredge Line text says colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus toward it, and Dark Procession creates terrain — so the old advice to 'wall his dredge escapes' actively hands him a free reposition. Placement rule is now stated consistently in five fields. Kit flag misfire noted as elsewhere: yorick.json tags Mourning Mist (E) 'dash'; Riot's text gives Yorick no movement (the speed goes to his summoned units), so no dash is asserted. Chart rows 1, 2 and 4 taken from the nautilus__yorick mirror; rows 0 and 3 taken from the packet chart, which this page's own whys already agreed with.
